plan: 2 Samuel 8:15-18; 1 Chronicles 18:14-17; 1 Chronicles 6:16-30, 50-53, 31-48; 2 Samuel 9:1-13; 2 Samuel 10:1-19; 1 Chronicles 19:1-19

readings.title: David Defeats the Philistines and Moabites
readings.subtitle: The Spoils of War
readings.text: [2 Samuel 8:1] And after this it came to be that Daviḏ struck <dn>את</dn> the Philistines and humbled them. And Daviḏ took <dn>את</dn> the bridle of the mother city out of the hand of the Philistines. [2] He also struck <dn>את</dn> Mo’aḇ, and measured them off with a line, causing them to lie down on the earth. With two lines he measured off those to be put to death, and with one complete line those to be kept alive. And the Mo’aḇites became Daviḏ’s servants, and brought presents. [3] Daviḏ also struck <dn>את</dn> Haḏaḏezer son of Reḥoḇ, sovereign of Tsoḇah, as he went to restore his rule at the River Euphrates. [4] And Daviḏ captured from him one thousand and seven hundred horsemen, and twenty thousand foot soldiers. And Daviḏ destroyed <dn>את</dn> all the chariots, but he left of them a hundred chariots. [5] And the Arameans of Dammeseq came to help Haḏaḏezer sovereign of Tsoḇah, and Daviḏ struck twenty-two thousand of the Arameans. [6] Then Daviḏ put watch-posts in Aram of Dammeseq. And the Arameans became Daviḏ’s servants, and brought presents. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> saved <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ wherever he went. [7] And Daviḏ took <dn>את</dn> the shields of gold which were on the servants of Haḏaḏezer, and brought them to Yerushalayim. [8] And from Betaḥ and from Běrothai, cities of Haḏaḏezer, Sovereign Daviḏ took very much bronze.

readings.title: To'i Sends Gifts to David
readings.subtitle: Dedicating the Spoils to YeHoVaH
readings.text: [9] And To‛i sovereign of Ḥamath heard that Daviḏ had stricken <dn>את</dn> all the army of Haḏaḏezer, [10] so To‛i sent <dn>את</dn> Yoram his son to Sovereign Daviḏ, to ask peace of him and bless him, because he had fought against Haḏaḏezer and struck him, for Haḏaḏezer had battles with To‛i. And Yoram brought with him objects of silver, and objects of gold, and objects of bronze. [11] Sovereign Daviḏ also set <dn>את</dn> these apart to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, along with the silver and gold that he had set apart from all the nations which he had humbled: [12] from Aram, and from Mo’aḇ, and from the children of Ammon, and from the Philistines, and from Amalěq, and from the spoil of Haḏaḏezer son of Reḥoḇ, sovereign of Tsoḇah. [13] And Daviḏ made a name for himself when he returned from striking <dn>את</dn> eighteen thousand Arameans in the Valley of Salt. [14] And he put watch-posts in Eḏom. Throughout all Eḏom he put watch-posts, and all the Eḏomites became Daviḏ’s servants. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> saved <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ wherever he went.

readings.title: David's Righteous Rule
readings.subtitle: The Officials of the Kingdom
readings.text: [15] And Daviḏ reigned over all Yisra’ěl, and Daviḏ was doing right-ruling and righteousness to all his people. [16] And Yo’aḇ son of Tseruyah was over the army, and Yehoshaphat son of Aḥiluḏ was recorder, [17] and Tsaḏoq son of Aḥituḇ and Aḥimeleḵ son of Eḇyathar were the priests, and Serayah was the scribe, [18] and Benayahu son of Yehoyaḏa was over both the Kerěthites and the Pelěthites, and Daviḏ’s sons were priests.

readings.title: David's Victories Over Aram and Zobah
readings.subtitle: Gathering Bronze for the Temple
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 18:1] And after this it came to be that Daviḏ struck <dn>את</dn> the Philistines, and humbled them, and took <dn>את</dn> Gath and <dn>את</dn> its towns from the hand of the Philistines. [2] And he struck <dn>את</dn> the Mo’aḇites, and the Mo’aḇites became Daviḏ’s servants, and brought presents. [3] And Daviḏ struck <dn>את</dn> Haḏaḏezer sovereign of Tsoḇah as far as Ḥamath, as he went to establish his power by the River Euphrates. [4] And Daviḏ took from him one thousand chariots, and seven thousand horsemen, and twenty thousand foot soldiers. And Daviḏ also hamstrung <dn>את</dn> all the chariot horses, but left of them for one hundred chariots. [5] And when Aram of Darmeseq came to help Haḏaḏezer sovereign of Tsoḇah, Daviḏ struck twenty-two thousand of Aram, [6] and Daviḏ stationed men in Aram of Darmeseq, and the Arameans became Daviḏ’s servants, and brought presents. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> saved <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ wherever he went. [7] And Daviḏ took <dn>את</dn> the shields of gold that were on the servants of Haḏaḏezer, and brought them to Yerushalayim. [8] And from Tiḇḥath and from Kun, cities of Haḏaḏezer, Daviḏ brought a large amount of bronze, with which Shelomoh made <dn>את</dn> the bronze Sea, and <dn>את</dn> the columns, and <dn>את</dn> the vessels of bronze.

readings.title: The King of Hamath Seeks Peace
readings.subtitle: Edom Becomes Subject to David
readings.text: [9] And when To‛u sovereign of Ḥamath heard that Daviḏ had stricken <dn>את</dn> all the army of Haḏaḏezer sovereign of Tsoḇah, [10] he sent <dn>את</dn> Haḏoram his son to Sovereign Daviḏ, to ask peace of him and bless him, because he had fought against Haḏaḏezer and struck him – because Haḏaḏezer had been fighting against To‛u – with all kinds of objects of gold, and silver, and bronze. [11] Sovereign Daviḏ also set <dn>את</dn> these apart to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, along with the silver and gold that he had brought from all these nations, from Eḏom, and from Mo’aḇ, and from the children of Ammon, and from the Philistines, and from Amalěq. [12] And Aḇishai son of Tseruyah struck <dn>את</dn> eighteen thousand Eḏomites in the Valley of Salt, [13] and he put watch-posts in Eḏom, and all the Eḏomites became Daviḏ’s servants. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> saved <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ wherever he went.

readings.title: The Administration of Israel
readings.subtitle: David's Chief Officials
readings.text: [14] So Daviḏ reigned over all Yisra’ěl, and he was doing right-ruling and righteousness to all his people. [15] And Yo’aḇ son of Tseruyah was over the army, and Yehoshaphat son of Aḥiluḏ was recorder, [16] and Tsaḏoq son of Aḥituḇ and Aḇimeleḵ son of Eḇyathar were the priests, and Shavsha was the scribe, [17] and Benayahu son of Yehoyaḏa was over the Kerěthites and the Pelěthites. And the sons of Daviḏ were chiefs at the sovereign’s side.

readings.title: David Seeks the House of Saul
readings.subtitle: Mephibosheth Brought Before the King
readings.text: [2 Samuel 9:1] And Daviḏ said, “Is there still anyone who is left of the house of Sha’ul, that I might show him loving-commitment, because of Yehonathan?” [2] And the house of Sha’ul had a servant whose name was Tsiḇa. And they had called <dn>את</dn> him to Daviḏ, and the sovereign said to him, “Are you Tsiḇa?” And he said, “Your servant!” [3] And the sovereign said, “Is there not still someone of the house of Sha’ul, so that I show him the loving-commitment of <dn>Elohim</dn>?” And Tsiḇa said to the sovereign, “There is still a son of Yehonathan, lame in his feet.” [4] So the sovereign said to him, “Where is he?” And Tsiḇa said to the sovereign, “See, he is in the house of Maḵir son of Ammi’ěl, in Lo Ḏeḇar.” [5] And Sovereign Daviḏ sent and brought him out of the house of Maḵir son of Ammi’ěl, from Lo Ḏeḇar. [6] And Mephiḇosheth son of Yehonathan, son of Sha’ul, came to Daviḏ, and fell on his face and did obeisance. And Daviḏ said, “Mephiḇosheth!” And he answered, “Here is your servant!” [7] Daviḏ then said to him, “Do not fear, for I shall certainly show you loving-commitment because of Yehonathan your father, and shall return to you <dn>את</dn> all the land of Sha’ul your grandfather, and let you eat bread at my table continually.” [8] And he bowed himself and said, “What is your servant, that you should turn to such a dead dog as I?”

readings.title: Restoring Saul's Land
readings.subtitle: A Place at the King's Table
readings.text: [9] And the sovereign called <dn>את</dn> Tsiḇa servant of Sha’ul, and said to him, “I have given to your master’s son <dn>את</dn> all that belonged to Sha’ul and to all his house. [10] “And you and your sons and your servants, shall work <dn>את</dn> the land for him, and you shall bring in its yield, and your master’s son shall have food to eat. But let Mephiḇosheth your master’s son eat bread at my table always.” And Tsiḇa had fifteen sons and twenty servants. [11] And Tsiḇa said to the sovereign, “According to all that my master the sovereign has commanded <dn>את</dn> his servant, so your servant does.” “As for Mephiḇosheth,” said the sovereign, “he shall eat at my table as one of the sons of the sovereign.” [12] And Mephiḇosheth had a young son whose name was Miḵa. And all who dwelt in the house of Tsiḇa were servants of Mephiḇosheth. [13] And Mephiḇosheth was dwelling in Yerushalayim, for he ate continually at the sovereign’s table. And he was lame in both his feet.

readings.title: The Ammonites Disgrace David's Messengers
readings.subtitle: Hanun's Foolish Provocation
readings.text: [2 Samuel 10:1] And after this it came to be that the sovereign of the children of Ammon died, and Ḥanun his son reigned in his place. [2] And Daviḏ said, “Let me show loving-commitment to Ḥanun son of Naḥash, as his father showed loving-commitment to me.” So Daviḏ sent by the hand of his servants to comfort him concerning his father. And when Daviḏ’s servants came into the land of the children of Ammon, [3] the chiefs of the children of Ammon said to Ḥanun their master, “Is Daviḏ esteeming <dn>את</dn> your father in your eyes in that he has sent comforters to you? Has Daviḏ not rather sent <dn>את</dn> his servants to you to search <dn>את</dn> the city, and to spy it out, and to overthrow it?” [4] So Ḥanun took <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ’s servants and shaved off half of their beards, and cut off <dn>את</dn> their garments in the middle, as far as their buttocks, and sent them away. [5] And they informed Daviḏ, and he sent to meet them, because the men were greatly ashamed. And the sovereign said, “Wait at Yeriḥo until your beards have grown, and then return.”

readings.title: The Ammonite and Aramean Alliance
readings.subtitle: Joab and Abishai Lead the Battle
readings.text: [6] And when the children of Ammon saw that they had become a stench to Daviḏ, the children of Ammon sent and hired <dn>את</dn> Arameans of Běyth Reḥoḇ and <dn>את</dn> Arameans of Tsoḇa, twenty thousand foot soldiers, and <dn>את</dn> the sovereign of Ma‛aḵah, one thousand men, and men of Toḇ, twelve thousand men. [7] And Daviḏ heard, and sent <dn>את</dn> Yo’aḇ and <dn>את</dn> the entire army, the mighty men. [8] And the children of Ammon came out and put themselves in battle array at the entrance of the gate. And the Arameans of Tsoḇa, and Reḥoḇ, and men of Toḇ, and Ma‛aḵah were by themselves in the field. [9] And Yo’aḇ saw that the battle line was against him before and behind, and he chose out of all the chosen men of Yisra’ěl and put them in battle array against the Arameans. [10] And <dn>את</dn> the rest of the people he gave under the hand of Aḇishai his brother, and he put them in battle array against the children of Ammon. [11] And he said, “If the Arameans are too strong for me, then you shall help me. But if the children of Ammon are too strong for you, then I shall come and help you. [12] “Be strong, and let us show strength for our people and for the cities of our <dn>Elohim</dn>, and let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> do what is good in <dn>His</dn> eyes.” [13] And Yo’aḇ drew near, and the people with him, to battle against Aram, and they fled before him. [14] And when the children of Ammon saw that the Arameans were fleeing, they also fled before Aḇishai, and went into the city. And Yo’aḇ returned from the children of Ammon and came to Yerushalayim.

readings.title: David Defeats the Aramean Reinforcements
readings.subtitle: The Arameans Make Peace
readings.text: [15] And Aram saw that they were smitten before Yisra’ěl, and they gathered together, [16] and Haḏaḏezer sent and brought out <dn>את</dn> the Arameans who were beyond the River, and they came to Ḥělam. And Shoḇaḵ the commander of the army of Haḏaḏezer went before them. [17] And it was reported to Daviḏ, and he gathered <dn>את</dn> all Yisra’ěl, and passed over <dn>את</dn> the Yarděn, and came to Ḥělam. And Aram set themselves in battle array against Daviḏ and they fought with him. [18] And Aram fled before Yisra’ěl, and Daviḏ killed seven hundred charioteers and forty thousand horsemen of Aram, and he struck <dn>את</dn> Shoḇaḵ, commander of their army, who died there. [19] And all the sovereigns, the servants of Haḏaḏezer, saw that they were smitten by Yisra’ěl, and made peace with <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl, and served them. And the Arameans were afraid to help <dn>את</dn> the children of Ammon any more.

readings.title: The Death of Nahash
readings.subtitle: David's Servants Humiliated
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 19:1] And after this it came to be that Naḥash the sovereign of the children of Ammon died, and his son reigned in his place. [2] And Daviḏ said, “Let me show loving-commitment to Ḥanun son of Naḥash, because his father showed loving-commitment to me.” So Daviḏ sent messengers to comfort him concerning his father. And the servants of Daviḏ came to Ḥanun in the land of the children of Ammon to comfort him. [3] And the chiefs of the children of Ammon said to Ḥanun, “Is Daviḏ esteeming <dn>את</dn> your father, in your eyes, because he has sent comforters to you? Have his servants not come to you to search and to overthrow and to spy out <dn>את</dn> the land?” [4] So Ḥanun took <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ’s servants, and shaved them, and cut off <dn>את</dn> their garments in the middle, at their buttocks, and sent them away. [5] And when some went and informed Daviḏ about the men, he sent to meet them, because the men were greatly ashamed. And the sovereign said, “Remain at Yeriḥo until your beards have grown, then return.”

readings.title: The Battle Against Ammon and Aram
readings.subtitle: Joab's Strategy for Victory
readings.text: [6] And when the children of Ammon saw that they had made themselves a stench to Daviḏ, Ḥanun and the children of Ammon sent a thousand talents of silver to hire chariots and horsemen from Aram-Naharayim, and from Aram-Ma‛aḵah, and from Tsoḇah. [7] So they hired for themselves thirty-two thousand chariots, with <dn>את</dn> the sovereign of Ma‛aḵah and <dn>את</dn> his people, who came and encamped before Měyḏeḇa. And the children of Ammon had gathered from their cities, and came to battle. [8] And when Daviḏ heard, he sent <dn>את</dn> Yo’aḇ and <dn>את</dn> the entire army of the mighty men, [9] and the children of Ammon came out and put themselves in battle array before the gate of the city, and the sovereigns who had come were by themselves in the field. [10] And when Yo’aḇ saw that the battle had been set against him before and behind, he chose some of the choice ones of Yisra’ěl, and put them in battle array to meet Aram. [11] And <dn>את</dn> the rest of the people he put under the command of Aḇishai his brother, and they set themselves in battle array to meet the children of Ammon. [12] And he said, “If Aram is too strong for me, then you shall help me; but if the children of Ammon are too strong for you, then I shall help you. [13] “Be strong, and let us show strength for our people and for the cities of our <dn>Elohim</dn>, and let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> do what is good in <dn>His</dn> eyes.” [14] And Yo’aḇ drew near, and the people with him, to battle against Aram, and they fled before him. [15] And when the children of Ammon saw that the Arameans were fleeing, they also fled before Aḇishai his brother, and went into the city. And Yo’aḇ came to Yerushalayim.

readings.title: The Final Defeat of Hadadezer
readings.subtitle: Aram Submits to Israel
readings.text: [16] And when Aram saw that they had been smitten before Yisra’ěl, they sent messengers and brought <dn>את</dn> the Arameans who were beyond the River, and Shophaḵ the commander of Haḏaḏezer’s army went before them. [17] And it was reported to Daviḏ, and he gathered <dn>את</dn> all Yisra’ěl, and passed over <dn>את</dn> the Yarděn and came upon them, and set up in battle array against them. And Daviḏ set up in battle array against Aram, and they fought with him. [18] And Aram fled before Yisra’ěl, and Daviḏ killed seven thousand charioteers and forty thousand foot soldiers of the Arameans, and smote <dn>את</dn> Shophaḵ the commander of the army. [19] And the servants of Haḏaḏezer saw that they were smitten by Yisra’ěl, and they made peace with <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ and became his servants. And the Arameans would not help <dn>את</dn> the children of Ammon any more.
